items.title: Palmeiras reach Copa Libertadores final after penalty shoot-out win
items.why: Brazil's Palmeiras beat Fluminense 5-3 on penalties in São Paulo on 21 October after their semi-final finished 2-2 on aggregate; Fluminense won the second leg 1-0. Goalkeeper Carlos Miguel saved Nonato's penalty and Marlon Freitas scored the winning kick.
items.matters: The final is in Montevideo, Uruguay, on 28 November against Flamengo or Estudiantes, who meet on Thursday.

items.title: Angel Reese leads Atlanta Dream to 2-1 lead in WNBA Finals
items.why: The Atlanta Dream beat the Golden State Valkyries 97-71 in Atlanta on Wednesday 21 October to lead the best-of-seven WNBA Finals 2-1. Angel Reese had 21 points and 12 rebounds in a sold-out arena; the Valkyries made only 35% of their shots.
items.matters: Game 4 is in Atlanta on Saturday; the Dream are two wins from their first WNBA title.

items.title: South Korea's central bank holds interest rate at 3% after two rises
items.why: The Bank of Korea kept its main interest rate at 3.00% on 22 October, a unanimous decision by its seven board members, after raising it in July and August. It said it wanted to watch how the earlier rises take effect; most analysts expect another rise in November.
items.matters: Booming chip exports are lifting South Korea's economy but adding to price pressures, Seoul Economic Daily reports.

items.title: North Korea to restart propaganda loudspeakers along the border with South Korea
items.why: Kim Yo Jong, sister of leader Kim Jong Un, said on Thursday loudspeakers would be on standby along the whole border within days and 'new counter means' on alert. South Korea says it fired warning shots when North Korean troops crossed the border during fortification work.
items.matters: South Korea's President Lee Jae Myung halted Seoul's own broadcasts last year to ease tensions; Seoul urges talks.

items.title: Tesla's profit falls 43% as car sales revenue slips
items.why: Tesla said on 21 October that third-quarter revenue was flat at $28.05 billion, slightly above forecasts, but net profit fell 43% to $787 million, partly because of a paper loss on its SpaceX stake. Revenue from car sales fell 3%.
items.matters: Elon Musk said a planned Tesla-SpaceX chip factory could cost over $100 billion, Investing.com reports.

items.title: Meta's sales jump 26% as it spends heavily on AI
items.why: Meta, owner of Facebook, Instagram and WhatsApp, said on 21 October that third-quarter revenue rose 26% to $64.6 billion. Profit was cut by a $9.89 billion charge for a settlement with 52 US states over teen mental health. It expects 2026 capital spending of $135–145 billion.
items.matters: Spending on AI data centres turned Meta's free cash flow negative, at minus $2.1 billion for the quarter, Fortune reports.

items.title: US orders non-emergency staff out of Saudi Arabia amid Houthi attacks
items.why: The US State Department on Wednesday ordered non-emergency staff and their families to leave Saudi Arabia, citing Houthi attacks on airports and infrastructure. Saudi aviation officials said an attack on Dammam's King Fahd airport, in the east, that evening killed one person and injured eight.
items.matters: Reuters reports other US Gulf missions will also send families home; the State Department calls reports of a Gulf-wide order 'inaccurate'.

items.title: Como beat Manchester United 4-1 in their first Champions League season
items.why: Italian club Como, coached by Cesc Fàbregas, beat Manchester United 4-1 in the Champions League at home in Como on 21 October. Nico Paz scored twice, with Tasos Douvikas and Jacobo Ramón also scoring; Joshua Zirkzee replied in stoppage time.
items.matters: United manager Michael Carrick apologised for an 'unacceptable' display; Como now have six points, United three.

items.title: US judge orders Meta to pay New Mexico $25 billion over privacy
items.why: A judge in Santa Fe, New Mexico, ordered Meta on 21 October to pay the state $25 billion after a jury found in September that it misled residents about data privacy, counting 43 million violations. The state had sought at least $35 billion. Meta says it will appeal.
items.matters: Meta had asked for no more than $3.45 billion and calls the penalty 'a tax on speech'.

items.title: Physicists hold a single antimatter particle in a trap for months
items.why: A Northwestern University team in the US has trapped one positron, the antimatter twin of the electron, and controlled its quantum states, they report in Physical Review Letters on 21 October. The particle can be held for months; loading one takes 8 to 11 hours.
items.matters: A precise measurement could test whether matter and antimatter truly mirror each other, part of why the universe has matter.

items.title: Governments take websites offline after two critical PHP security flaws
items.why: PHP, the programming language behind most websites, released emergency fixes on 21 October for two flaws that can let attackers run code on servers remotely. The Netherlands, Denmark, France and Finland took some government sites offline as a precaution, Reuters reports; Canada did too.
items.matters: Website owners must update PHP; its developers say there is no complete workaround, and South Korea has issued an emergency alert.

items.title: Qatar, Türkiye, Pakistan and Indonesia sign 'Badr' defence industry pact
items.why: Defence ministers and officials of the four countries signed the 'Badr' memorandum in Qatar's capital, Doha, on Wednesday, Türkiye's defence ministry said. It covers joint weapons production, training, and research and development. It does not include a mutual defence pledge.
items.matters: Al Jazeera sees it as part of a wider push for new security ties in the region during the war with Iran.

items.title: UN warns El Niño could be the strongest on record
items.why: The World Meteorological Organization says tropical Pacific temperatures may reach 3.8C above average between November and January; its chief says record El Niños have reached about 3C. In Geneva on 21 October, UN aid chief Tom Fletcher released over $50 million for 11 countries, including Chad, Ethiopia and Somalia.
items.matters: Fletcher says about 50 million people could face increased hunger as heat, drought and floods hit.

items.title: WHO launches global indicators to track heat risks for mothers and children
items.why: The World Health Organization, with the WMO, UNICEF and the UN Population Fund, published on 21 October the first global set of indicators for how extreme heat affects pregnant women, newborns and children. It links heat exposure to 26% higher odds of preterm birth.
items.matters: WHO says about 1.5 billion children face heatwaves that are more frequent, longer or more severe.

items.title: Indonesia holds main interest rate, lifts deposit rate to support rupiah
items.why: Bank Indonesia kept its main rate at 5.75% on 21 October but raised its deposit facility rate to 5% and will cut banks' reserve requirements, freeing about 190 trillion rupiah ($10.6 billion). The rupiah, down more than 7% this year, is near 18,000 per dollar.
items.matters: It follows MSCI's warning it may downgrade Indonesia's stock market, which set off the country's steepest share fall in decades.

items.title: Mexico holds ex-prosecutor on treason charge over US agents in drug raid
items.why: A federal judge has ordered César Jáuregui, former attorney general of Mexico's northern Chihuahua state, held in pre-trial detention. Prosecutors accuse him of letting US agents, reported to be CIA officers, join an April drug-lab raid without federal approval. His defence calls the case political.
items.matters: Mexico rarely brings treason charges; the case tests limits on US security operations inside Mexico.

items.title: UK inflation rises to 3.5%, its highest in almost a year
items.why: Prices in the UK rose 3.5% in the year to September, up from 3.1% in August and above the 3.4% most economists expected, the Office for National Statistics said on 21 October. Petrol and diesel drove the rise; diesel is at its highest since July 2022.
items.matters: Motor fuel prices are up nearly 30% on a year ago, the ONS says, raising costs for households and businesses.

items.title: UN says world heads for 2.6C warming even if pledges are met
items.why: The UN Environment Programme's Emissions Gap Report, published on 21 October, says fully delivering countries' climate pledges would still mean about 2.6C of warming by 2100; current policies point to 2.8C. Global emissions were about 58.4 billion tonnes in 2025, roughly level with 2024.
items.matters: UNEP says emissions must fall 18% by 2030 to keep the overshoot above 1.5C as small as possible.

items.title: LeBron James's 76ers spoil Knicks' title celebration as NBA season opens
items.why: The Philadelphia 76ers beat the champion New York Knicks 106-100 at Madison Square Garden on 20 October, the NBA's opening night, after the Knicks raised their first title banner in 53 years. LeBron James, in a record 24th season, had 14 points on his 76ers debut; Tyrese Maxey scored 28.

items.changed: Updated: the Kospi fell back more than 2% on Thursday after Wednesday's rebound
items.title: Asian shares fall again as doubts over AI spending hit chipmakers
items.why: After Wednesday's 3.3% rebound, Seoul's Kospi fell more than 2% on Thursday morning, with Samsung Electronics and SK hynix down over 3%. Hong Kong's Hang Seng dropped about 2.5% and Tokyo's Nikkei 1.1%. Mixed results from Tesla and Meta revived doubts over AI investment returns, AFP reports.
items.matters: Korean chipmakers are a bellwether for global spending on artificial intelligence.

items.title: Skeleton in Roman coffin at Westminster Abbey was probably a Saxon abbot
items.why: A skeleton found in a fourth-century Roman sarcophagus at Westminster Abbey in London is most likely Ælfwig, an abbot who died around 1020, the abbey's consultant archaeologist Warwick Rodwell argues in the Journal of the British Archaeological Association. Radiocarbon dating places the man's death between 987 and 1052.
items.matters: The coffin's inscription names a fourth-century Briton, so it was reused centuries later; Rodwell names a second candidate, Wulfnoth.

items.title: Musk says SpaceX and Tesla have formed committees to consider merging
items.why: Elon Musk said on 20 October that SpaceX and Tesla have each set up committees of independent directors to discuss combining, calling it 'a good idea' but not certain. SpaceX, which listed in June, reported a $4.4 billion quarterly profit on revenue up 161% to $14.6 billion.
items.matters: Al Jazeera says the two firms are worth about $3.5 trillion together, so a deal would be the largest merger ever.

items.title: PSG beat Barcelona 4-2, ending their winning start to the season
items.why: Champions League holders Paris Saint-Germain beat Barcelona 4-2 in Paris on 20 October, with late goals from Vitinha and Fabián Ruiz after Lamine Yamal had made it 2-2. It ended Barcelona's run of 11 straight wins; PSG have nine points from three league-phase games.

items.title: Liverpool come from two goals down to beat Villarreal 4-3
items.why: Liverpool beat Villarreal 4-3 in the Champions League at Anfield on 20 October after trailing 2-0 within 29 minutes. Alexis Mac Allister scored twice, with Ronald Araújo and substitute Florian Wirtz also scoring; 18-year-old Rio Ngumoha set up two goals.

items.title: Netflix shares fall after weak forecast and cut to advertising outlook
items.why: Netflix said on 20 October its third-quarter revenue rose 12% to $12.9 billion, in line with forecasts, but it predicted lower fourth-quarter profit than analysts expected and cut its 2026 advertising revenue forecast to about $2.7 billion from $3 billion. Shares fell nearly 6% in after-hours trading.
items.matters: The company recently cut about 1,000 jobs, around 6% of staff, and replaced its content chief, Reuters reports.

items.changed: Updated: electoral court meets Meta and both campaigns over equal treatment online
items.title: Brazil's electoral court meets Meta and both campaigns before Sunday's run-off
items.why: A judge at Brazil's Superior Electoral Court met Meta and lawyers for President Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro on Tuesday over an order to treat both candidates equally online. Lula's campaign says its posts were restricted; Meta denies favouring either side and blames technical faults. The run-off is on 25 October.
items.matters: It tests how far courts can police tech platforms during an election.

items.title: US approves first drug of its kind for chronic hepatitis B
items.why: The US Food and Drug Administration approved GSK's Hibsago (bepirovirsen) on 20 October for some adults with chronic hepatitis B, given alongside existing antivirals. In two trials, 19% of patients still had the virus under control six months after stopping all treatment; none did on placebo.
items.matters: GSK says more than 240 million people live with chronic hepatitis B, which causes about 1.1 million deaths a year.

items.title: US regulator approves Boeing's largest 737 Max after years of delays
items.why: The US Federal Aviation Administration certified the Boeing 737 Max 10 on 20 October, almost a decade after the jet was unveiled in 2017. It seats up to 230 passengers. More than 30 customers have ordered 1,555, and Boeing expects deliveries to begin in the coming months.
items.matters: It is the first airliner certified under all of a 2020 US safety law passed after two 737 Max crashes.

items.title: Rare Arctic beluga whale filmed off Ireland's Donegal coast
items.why: A beluga whale, normally found in Arctic and sub-Arctic waters, was filmed by drone in Donegal Bay, north-west Ireland, on 17 October. The Irish Whale and Dolphin Group says it is only the second validated beluga record in Irish waters, after one off County Antrim in 2015.
items.matters: The group says the adult appears healthy, and Arctic species such as belugas and narwhals are being seen more often off Ireland.

items.changed: Updated: Guards now say they struck four more ships and three others hit mines
items.title: Iran's Revolutionary Guards say they hit seven more ships in the Gulf
items.why: Iran's Revolutionary Guards navy said on Thursday it struck four ships transferring oil in the northern Gulf, setting them on fire, and that three more hit mines west of the Strait of Hormuz. It warned the US that its regional bases could be targeted. The claims are not independently confirmed.
items.matters: Before the war about a fifth of the world's oil passed through the strait.

items.changed: Updated: Putin agrees to resume three-way talks after 10 November and frees a US prisoner
items.title: Putin agrees to resume Ukraine peace talks after meeting Witkoff
items.why: Russia's President Putin met US envoy Steve Witkoff for about three hours in St Petersburg on Wednesday. Kremlin aide Yuri Ushakov said Russia agreed in principle to resume three-way talks with Ukraine and the US after 10 November, possibly in Abu Dhabi. Russia freed US citizen Stephen Hubbard.
items.matters: Ushakov said Western and Ukrainian proposals offered 'little' of use; Zelensky says freezing the front line is the minimum.

items.title: Italy sends 500 soldiers to Milan and toughens protest laws after riots
items.why: Italy's cabinet approved a decree on Tuesday sending 500 extra soldiers to Milan until the end of the year, after weekend riots and looting during cost-of-living protests. It creates an offence of 'violent participation in a demonstration', punishable by up to five years in prison.
items.matters: It follows similar fuel-price unrest in France, where night curfews remain in parts of Paris and Lyon.

items.title: Christina Applegate says doctors now find she does not have MS
items.why: US actor Christina Applegate, 54, who announced a multiple sclerosis diagnosis in 2021, said on her podcast MeSsy on 20 October that her doctor has told her she does not have the disease. She still has severe symptoms and says she is 'back at square one'.
items.matters: A Cedars-Sinai neurologist on the podcast said misdiagnosis of MS is fairly common, as there is no single test for it.

items.title: Arafat Minhas takes six wickets as Pakistan beat England by 87 runs
items.why: All-rounder Arafat Minhas scored 59 and took six wickets for 40 as Pakistan beat England by 87 runs in a one-day tri-series match in Rawalpindi, Pakistan, on 20 October. Pakistan made 302 for nine; England were bowled out for 215.

items.title: UN experts urge India to stop 'excessive force' against protesters
items.why: About two dozen independent UN human rights experts said on Tuesday that police used baton charges on unarmed students at protests in New Delhi and elsewhere. They cite reports that more than 7,000 people were detained. Protesters want India's chief election commissioner to resign over voter-list revisions.
items.matters: Critics say about 130 million names were removed from voter lists; the Election Commission says it removed ineligible voters.

items.changed: Updated: Australia were bowled out for 99 and made to follow on
items.title: Australia bowled out for 99 and follow on in second Test
items.why: Marco Jansen took five for 33 as Australia were bowled out for 99 on day four in Gqeberha, South Africa, on 21 October, 326 behind. Following on, they closed on 156 for four, still 170 behind, with Travis Head 87 not out. Australia lead the series 1-0.
items.matters: Day five is on Thursday 22 October; South Africa need six more wickets to level the three-match series.

items.changed: Updated: Brent back above $110 after Houthi attacks in Saudi Arabia
items.title: Oil rises above $110 a barrel after attacks in Saudi Arabia
items.why: Brent crude rose about 1.5% to above $110 a barrel early on Thursday after Houthi drone attacks in Saudi Arabia, including near Aramco's Shaybah oilfield, The National and AFP report. It had settled almost flat near $108.8 on Wednesday. The US ordered non-emergency staff to leave Saudi Arabia.
items.matters: Oil prices feed into fuel, heating and shipping costs around the world.

items.title: Rubio says US and India are 'very close' to a trade deal
items.why: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio met India's Foreign Minister S Jaishankar in Mumbai on Tuesday, AP reports. Rubio said a deal is 'about as close as you can be' without signing. Talks have stalled for months over US tariffs and India's purchases of Russian oil.
items.matters: US tariffs on Indian goods reached 50% in 2025 before a February framework cut them to 18%.

items.title: Britain to fly RAF Typhoon jets to defend Saudi Arabia from Houthis
items.why: Britain's Ministry of Defence said on Tuesday that RAF Typhoons will fly defensive missions over Saudi Arabia against Houthi drones and missiles, after a Saudi request. They will not strike Houthi targets in Yemen. Defence Secretary Wes Streeting called the Houthi attacks 'absolutely despicable'.
items.matters: It deepens Britain's military role as Houthi strikes on Saudi cities, airports and oil sites continue.

items.title: South Africa's Transnet claims world record with 7.6 km freight train
items.why: State rail company Transnet says a train of 696 empty wagons, 7.6 km long, ran about 861 km from Saldanha port to the iron ore mines of the Northern Cape over the weekend of 17-18 October. The previous record, per Guinness, was BHP's 7.35 km train in Australia in 2001.
items.matters: The claim has not yet been independently verified; Transnet's rail chief says the technical lessons matter more than the record.

items.changed: Updated: Trump says the US is 'not negotiating'; NYT reports plans for renewed strikes
items.title: Trump says US is 'not negotiating' with Iran as mediation stalls
items.why: President Trump told reporters on Wednesday the US is 'not negotiating' with Iran and that something will happen 'fairly soon'. The New York Times reports US and Israeli plans for renewed strikes after the 3 November midterms; the White House does not comment. Iran insists on its seven conditions.
items.matters: Iran says the Strait of Hormuz, a key oil route, stays shut until its terms are met; Pakistan is mediating.

items.changed: Updated: Champi has weakened slightly; Taiwan has issued a sea warning
items.title: Super Typhoon Champi weakens slightly as Taiwan issues sea warning
items.why: Champi, called Rosal in the Philippines, had winds of 195 km/h early on Thursday 22 October, about 495 km east of Batanes, the Philippine weather agency PAGASA says. Batanes and the Babuyan Islands remain under Signal No. 2; closest approach is Thursday afternoon to Friday morning.
items.matters: Taiwan's weather agency expects the strongest effects on Friday and Saturday; some ferries and Taiwan–Okinawa flights are cancelled.

items.title: Four Salvadoran soldiers missing after gang ambush in Haiti
items.why: Gangs attacked an armoured vehicle of the UN-backed Gang Suppression Force on Sunday in Croix-des-Bouquets, near Haiti's capital, Port-au-Prince, El Salvador's military says. Four Salvadoran air force members escaped the burning vehicle but remain unaccounted for; helicopters sent to help came under fire.
items.matters: AP calls it the first major attack on the force, which has about 2,000 troops, just over a third of its target.

items.changed: Updated: toll rises to at least 73
items.title: Yemen officials say Houthi missiles killed at least 73 at army camp
items.why: Houthi ballistic missiles hit a government training camp near Ataq, in Shabwa province, southern Yemen, on Monday. A senior government official told AP at least 73 recruits were killed; the governor says more than 200 were wounded and some are missing. The Houthis said they targeted 'Saudi enemy' forces.
items.matters: AP calls it the deadliest strike since fighting in Yemen escalated in July.

items.changed: Updated: drone strike on Abyei market; local officials say at least 153 killed
items.title: Officials say drone strike on Abyei market killed at least 153
items.why: A drone hit Amiet market and a nearby fuel depot in Abyei, an area claimed by both Sudan and South Sudan, on Monday. Abyei's information minister says at least 153 people died and later put the toll above 220. He and South Sudan's government blame Sudan's army.
items.matters: A Sudanese army officer told AP the army targeted fuel bound for the paramilitary RSF and does not target civilians.

items.changed: Updated: man charged and remanded in custody; her husband says she is stable
items.title: Man charged over car attack on Australian MP Helen Haines
items.why: Independent MP Helen Haines, 65, was hit by a four-wheel drive outside her office in Wangaratta, Victoria, on Monday. A 43-year-old man appeared in court on Wednesday charged with intentionally causing serious injury and harming a Commonwealth official, and was remanded in custody.
items.matters: Her husband says she is seriously injured but stable; police have not ruled out further charges.

items.changed: Updated: Congo's figures rose to more than 9,500 cases and 4,500 deaths
items.title: Nigeria confirms first Ebola case as Kenya's total rises to nine
items.why: Nigeria's health ministry said on 20 October that a woman who arrived in the capital, Abuja, from Uganda has Ebola; 44 contacts are being monitored. Kenya has nine confirmed cases, all in one cluster. Congo has recorded more than 9,500 cases and 4,500 deaths, its health ministry says.
items.matters: WHO says Nigeria is the fifth country to detect this Bundibugyo strain, for which there is no licensed vaccine.

items.changed: Updated: police say the actor was not the gunmen's first target
items.title: Police say Tiger Shroff was not the gunmen's original target
items.why: Mumbai's Crime Branch says the men who fired at actor Tiger Shroff's car on 18 October first planned to attack another film star but found his security too tight. Three suspects arrested in Kota, Rajasthan, were brought to Mumbai on 21 October; Delhi Police arrested four more.
